full_judgment:
Md Rezaul Haque J: This Civil Rule No. 425(f) of 2004 under section 5, Limitation Act (arising out of FAT No. 228/2004) was issued at the instance the defendants-appellants-petitioner calling upon plaintiff respondents opposite parties Nos. 1-5 to show cause as to why delay of 279 day (in fact 243 days) in preferring FAT No. 228/2004 against Judgment and decree dated 10-5-2003, decree signed 17-5-2003 in TS No. 108/2002 by Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur should not be condoned or to pass such order or orders as the Court may deem fit and proper. 

 3. Stating above facts application under section 5, Limitation Act accompanied by affidavit having been sworn on 19-5-2004 as above was filed for condonation of said delay. Subsequently supplementary affidavit was filed on behalf of defendants-appellants-petitioners stating some more facts with regard to appeal itself. 

 18. It is not disputed that procedural process has to be passed through in order to prepare memo of appeal to be filed on behalf of Government and in going through such processes concerned file has to be sent to different authorities for opinion, comment, sanction and approval. During such processes time is consumed. It is true that prompt and intelligent dealing with file by office of each authority may save time but from experiences it appears that different authorities do not carefully, efficiently and intelligently deal with such file wherein question of limitation is always involved.
